title: Continuation rules
summary: Future NORM work must preserve socket isolation and be qualified against the current common provider estate rather than forking a NORM-specific application API.
invariants: Before changing NORM, check the current SocketProvider and Network Transport Intentions baselines and re-run the common selector/member/readiness contracts.
Do not add NORM-specific branches to LDAP, Queue Fabric, NotNotes or other callers; callers declare communication requirements and SocketSelector chooses among current qualified offers.
Do not move XTP route/multipath/pacing logic, NORM NACK/FEC logic, QUIC TLS mechanics or RFC multicast syscalls into the common provider.
Next useful NORM work is Event Runtime registration and simultaneous multi-membership/multi-interface qualification; preserve explicit membership lifetime and full address identity.
Any future COTS/libnorm version change requires fresh native and wire qualification; do not infer compatibility from header shape alone.
